title: Out-of-the-money call spreads for leveraged upside on names you like
summary: The speaker uses one-year out-of-the-money call spreads on stocks he likes to add leverage in a tactical sleeve. The Lululemon example needs the stock near $250 within a year. He describes it as roughly 10 to 1 leverage on the stock. If the stock does not get there, the whole premium is lost, so size it small.

steps.caption: Lululemon trades near $200 in this example. The view is bullish over one year.
Buy the lower call and sell the $250 call, both out of the money, one year out.
At expiry the spread pays its full width if the stock is above $250.
If right, the return on premium is large: the speaker calls it about 10 to 1 leverage on the stock move.
Breakeven is the long strike plus the debit paid.
Below the long strike at expiry you lose 100% of the premium. Size it as a full loss.
Before expiry the spread moves less than the stock; most of the payoff comes late.

takeaways: An OTM call spread gives leveraged upside with a defined maximum loss.
Use it in a small tactical sleeve on names you already like.
Size each trade so a 100% loss of premium is acceptable.
caveats: The transcript is partly cut: the exact strikes and cost are not stated. The strikes here are illustrative.
Not a trade recommendation (the speaker says this too). The waitlist and tools are promotional.

backtest.note: One-year OTM call spread, about 40/20 delta, small risk per trade, hold for the move or the full loss.
